newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta international banks see rapid growth.
newsitem.headline: Malta international banks see rapid growth.

text.p: International banking institutions represented in Malta saw continued rapid growth of their consolidated balance sheet last year, Malta's Central Bank said.

In its annual report for 1996 released late on Monday, it said the institutions' assets and liabilities rose by 260.6 million Malta pounds ($681.33 million), or 63.9 percent from 1995 to reach to 668.4 million pounds ($1747.53m) at the end of the December.

The Central Bank said the foreign assets of international banking institutions in Malta nearly doubled in 1996 to 462.9 million pounds, mostly due to buoyant growth in advances to non-residents and holdings in foreign securities.
Claims on deposit money banks rose to 200.3 million pounds from 162.1 million pounds.
Deposits belonging to non-residents increased by 103.6 million to 280.1 million pounds.
Other liabilities rose by 67 million pounds to 101.6 million while capital and reserves were up by 24 percent to 33.1 million pounds.
Eight international banking institutions were operating in Malta at the end of 1996, of which Bank of Valletta International and Mid-Med Overseas are subsidiaries of local banks.
The other institutions were First Austrian Bank, First International Merchant Bank, Izola Bank, Turkiye Garanti Bankasi AG, Volksbank (Malta) and Investkredit International Bank.
GiroCredit Bank Malta and Austrian Raiffeisen Malta Bank were granted a banking licence late last year.
